summary: Backend-only iteration 75 tests — all 10 tests PASSED (100%). Covered: (1) device-scoped anonymous auth via POST /api/auth/anonymous with optional device_id — same device+same nickname returns same user_id, same device+different nickname preserves user_id but updates nickname (verified via DB), different device_ids yield different user_ids, missing/empty device_id keeps legacy fresh-user behaviour; (2) owner-scoped comment ordering on GET /api/feuds/{feud_id}/comments?owner_user_id=X — owner's comments float to a new topmost bucket for authenticated viewers, no owner_user_id falls back to existing bucketing (viewer's own comment outranks the owner), owner_user_id==viewer does not hide the viewer's own comment, anonymous viewers also see owner's comments first; (3) POST /api/admin/generate-daily smoke test with count=1 returns 200 with the expected {'created': [...]} shape after the recent-feuds prompt-context addition — no crash.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:890 trims device_id to 120 chars — the truncated value is then persisted, so two different device_ids that share the same first 120 chars would collide onto the same anonymous account. Realistic client UUIDs are 36 chars, so risk is negligible; noting for the record.

server.py:2664-2678 anonymous+owner_user_id fallback sorts only by (owner_first, recency) and does not preserve the reply_count popularity ordering used elsewhere for non-owner comments. Minor UX inconsistency vs the authenticated path, but matches the intended lightweight behaviour.
server.py:2634 owner-bucket logic uses `uid != viewer_id` guard so the viewer's own comment stays in bucket 0 even when the viewer is the profile owner — good defensive coding, verified by test_c.
seed_data_creation: Test-scoped ephemeral users created via /api/auth/signup and /api/auth/anonymous. Anonymous test users tagged with device_id='TEST-dev-<uuid>' are deleted in teardown. Test comments prefixed with 'TEST_' are best-effort deleted in teardown_class. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iter74_device_and_owner_comments.py covers device-scoped anon auth, owner_user_id comment ordering, and generate-daily smoke. Run with `pytest backend/tests/test_iter74_device_and_owner_comments.py -v`. Note: the generate-daily test can take 30-60s due to the LLM+fact-check chain; timeout is set to 180s.
